{"id": 176, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — Talvern Logistics litigation hold notice to ESI custodians (2025-05-06)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "TALVERN LOGISTICS GROUP LLC — OFFICE OF THE GENERAL COUNSEL
LITIGATION HOLD NOTICE — PRIVILEGED PORTIONS REDACTED; PRODUCED PURSUANT TO COURT ORDER OF SEPTEMBER 4, 2025
Date of issuance: May 6, 2025
From: S. Marchetti, General Counsel and Secretary
To: Distribution list of eighteen custodians, including D. Kessler (VP Operations), R. Okafor (Site Manager, Complex 4), P. Natarajan (Regional Energy Desk), N. Grieve (CFO)

Re: PRESERVATION OBLIGATION — Meridian Grain Cooperative dispute, Silo Complex 4

You are receiving this notice because the company reasonably anticipates litigation with Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. arising from grain storage conditions at Silo Complex 4, Halden Junction, under the Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement dated August 1, 2023. On May 5, 2025 the company received a preservation demand from the cooperative's counsel. Effective immediately upon your receipt of this notice, you must preserve, and must not delete, alter, overwrite or discard, the categories of information described below, in whatever form held.

Categories to preserve: (1) all communications, in any medium including email, chat, text message and voicemail, concerning climate control, dehumidification, humidity, energy usage, load-shedding or maintenance at Silo Complex 4, from January 1, 2025 forward; (2) site diaries, annunciator and alarm logs, controller data, and sensor or data-logger records for Complex 4; (3) documents concerning the Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement, including performance, monitoring and specification compliance; (4) documents concerning cost containment measures affecting leased storage sites; and (5) documents concerning the condition, grading or disposition of grain stored at Complex 4.

IT actions: as of the date of this notice, information technology has been directed to suspend automatic deletion, journaling expiry and mailbox retention cycling for all custodians on the distribution list, and to sequester existing backup media within the covered date range. Custodians must not rely on those systems in place of personal compliance.

This obligation continues until you receive written release from this office. Questions should be directed to the undersigned and not discussed with other custodians. Acknowledgment of receipt is required within three business days by return email.

S. Marchetti
General Counsel and Secretary, Talvern Logistics Group LLC"}

{"id": 164, "title": "Discovery-retrieval pack — TLG-EM-0414 email thread: Kessler to Okafor, Complex 4 load-shed directive (2025-03-14)", "doc_type": "input_materials", "related_shape": "discovery-retrieval", "body": "PRODUCED FROM CUSTODIAN MAILBOX: d.kessler@talvernlogistics.example — Bates TLG-EM-0414 through TLG-EM-0416
CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877

---- Message 3 of 3 ----
From: Dana Kessler, VP Operations, Talvern Logistics Group LLC
To: Ruth Okafor, Site Manager, Silo Complex 4 (Halden Junction)
Cc: Priya Natarajan, Regional Energy Desk
Date: Friday, March 14, 2025, 4:47 PM CT
Subject: RE: RE: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Ruth — decision is made. Effective tonight, take dehumidification units DH-4A, DH-4B, DH-4C and DH-4D at Complex 4 offline on the load-shed schedule, 22:00 to 06:00, and if the demand-charge numbers hold, keep them dark through the shoulder season. Priya's model says Complex 4 climate control is 61 percent of the site's demand charge and we are not clawing back the Q1 overrun any other way.

I am aware of what the Meridian contract says. Section 6.2 of the Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement calls for continuous dehumidification and a ceiling of 55 percent relative humidity in the storage galleries. If Meridian asks, this is routine maintenance on the air-handling side. Log it that way in the site diary. I will take the heat if Meridian notices.

Do not route this through the maintenance ticketing queue — handle it as a local operating instruction from this office.

— DK

---- Message 2 of 3 ----
From: Ruth Okafor
To: Dana Kessler
Date: Friday, March 14, 2025, 3:58 PM CT
Subject: RE: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Dana — before I touch those units I want it in writing. The galleries are holding 1.04 million bushels of Meridian hard red spring wheat right now and the loggers have us at 52 to 54 percent RH with all four units running. If we shed them overnight in March we will drift over spec within days. Please confirm you are directing the power-down notwithstanding the WCSA humidity clause.

---- Message 1 of 3 ----
From: Priya Natarajan, Regional Energy Desk
To: Dana Kessler
Date: Thursday, March 13, 2025, 11:12 AM CT
Subject: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Dana — attached is the demand-charge workup. Complex 4 is the outlier in the region. The only lever big enough this quarter is the dehumidification bank. Flagging for your call; this desk does not have authority over leased-site climate equipment."}
